scenes.speaker: alice
scenes.text: Welcome back to the show. Today we are diving into something serious.

scenes.speaker: bob
scenes.text: The gender wars. It is not just internet drama anymore.

scenes.speaker: alice
scenes.text: Right. It is actually changing how people form relationships.

scenes.speaker: bob
scenes.text: And the data is alarming. Look at South Korea.

scenes.speaker: alice
scenes.text: Their birth rate dropped to zero point seven two. That is the lowest in the world.

scenes.speaker: bob
scenes.text: Japan is not far behind at one point two. Both countries are shrinking.

scenes.speaker: alice
scenes.text: Young men and women are literally not dating anymore. They have given up.

scenes.speaker: bob
scenes.text: In Korea, there is a movement called the four B movement.

scenes.speaker: alice
scenes.text: No dating, no sex, no marriage, no childbirth. Women are opting out entirely.

scenes.speaker: bob
scenes.text: And men are responding with their own movements. The divide is growing.

scenes.speaker: alice
scenes.text: Social media amplifies the extreme voices on both sides.

scenes.speaker: bob
scenes.text: Every disagreement becomes a battle. Every relationship becomes a power struggle.

scenes.speaker: alice
scenes.text: The result? Loneliness epidemics in both genders.

scenes.speaker: bob
scenes.text: Marriage rates have cratered. Birth rates are collapsing across developed nations.

scenes.speaker: alice
scenes.text: This is not a left or right issue. It is a human issue.

scenes.speaker: bob
scenes.text: When men and women see each other as enemies, society breaks down.

scenes.speaker: alice
scenes.text: The population decline in Korea and Japan is just the beginning.

scenes.speaker: bob
scenes.text: We need to find a way back to mutual understanding. Before it is too late.
